editorial.subjectLine: Twelve teams, two days, one AI hackathon
editorial.previewText: The venue prize went to kailine — and on 3 September we're at Les Mills Auckland City for the next one.

founderNote.heading: A note from our founder
founderNote.bodyMd:
A few weeks ago we wrapped up our AI Hackathon at AUT's City Campus, run with the AI Forum New Zealand and AUT as part of the Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival. 129 people registered, more than 30 mentors gave their time, and over two days teams built real solutions to real problems across sustainability, accessibility, health and workforce challenges. What stayed with me was watching people move AI from conversation into action. They took problems that matter to their communities and, in two days, built something that worked.

Our next event is this week at Les Mills, and we would love to see you there. These evenings are where our community comes together to learn, share what we are working on, and meet people walking a similar path. Whether you are just starting out or well into your career, there is a place for you in the room.

None of this happens without you. Every person who shows up, mentors, asks a question or brings a friend is part of why She Sharp keeps growing. Thank you for being part of it, and I hope to see you this week.
founderNote.signature: Dr. Mahsa McCauley, Founder & Chair, She Sharp

headline.blurb: An evening at Les Mills Auckland City on diversity and AI for impact: a cross-functional panel, table discussions, and enough time afterwards to actually meet the people in the room.

photoOfTheMonth.alt: Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival 2026 — AUT City Campus

editorial.recapIntro: August was a single event that filled two whole days — here is how it went at AUT.

eventBlurbs.aotearoa-ai-hackathon-festival-2026:
Twelve teams spent Friday evening and all of Saturday in the Sir Paul Reeves Building at AUT City Campus, building AI solutions to real problems. Around a third of them had never been to a hackathon before, and mentors from AUT, She Sharp, Fisher & Paykel Healthcare and Southern Cross Health Society worked alongside the teams across both days.

On Saturday afternoon each team had five minutes in WG308 in front of a local judging panel. kailine took the venue prize, with kaitiakidata and kpi-kaitiaki-positive-impact as runners-up. The winning pitch goes on to national judging, and the national finalists pitch at the Aotearoa AI Summit in Wellington on 8–9 September.

opportunities.title: Become a mentor
opportunities.body: The mentors at the hackathon did not build anything for anyone. They asked better questions, and teams got unstuck. That is most of the job, and a few hours a month is enough to do it.

opportunities.title: Volunteer with us
opportunities.body: Two days at AUT ran on people who set up rooms, kept the kai coming, and noticed the person standing on their own. September's panel is the next one that needs you.

opportunities.title: Support the mahi
opportunities.body: Our events are free to attend, which is a decision someone has to pay for. A donation of any size keeps the door open for the next person walking through it.

editorial.sponsorThanks: Two days at AUT City Campus took a lot of people. Thank you to AUT for the building and the rooms, to AI Forum New Zealand for running the festival nationally, and to AWS behind the prizes. Thank you also to Fisher & Paykel Healthcare, Woolworths New Zealand with Kai Commitment, and My Life My Voice for putting real problems in front of the teams, and to Seen Ventures for the free Hack Fit training in the weeks beforehand.
